questions.text: When may an architect safely claim a professional specialization under Section 1-f?

options.text: When the claim is supported by well-known facts or professional consensus and years of experience
Whenever the architect has completed one related project
Whenever a client approves the advertisement
Whenever the claim appears in paid publicity

rationale.correct: Section 1-f allows specialization claims only when backed by well-known facts or professional consensus and years of experience.
rationale.takeaway: Section 1-f allows specialization claims only when backed by well-known facts or professional consensus and years of experience.

questions.explanation: Publication prestige does not fulfill the Code's specific requirement for professional consensus and academic/experience backing. [cite: 98] External recognition is valuable, but the Code requires specialization claims to be substantiated facts sanctioned by the profession. [cite: 98] The prohibition is on exaggerated or misleading publicity; the lack of payment doesn't make an unsubstantiated specialization claim valid. [cite: 98, 126] Specialization claims require professional consensus and substantiated years of experience; individual media recognition is not equivalent to professional consensus. [cite: 90, 98] Misrepresenting qualifications by claiming specialization without substantiated professional consensus is an ethical violation. [cite: 90, 94, 98]

questions.text: A client asks an architect to remove a safety measure to reduce cost. Which Section 1 answer is safest?

options.text: Follow the client because the client pays the fee
Keep the answer anchored to the architect duty to advance safety, health, and well-being
Treat the issue only as a contractor preference
Ignore laws and regulations if the project is private

rationale.correct: Section 1-a supports safety, health, and well-being as public responsibilities.
rationale.takeaway: Section 1-a supports safety, health, and well-being as public responsibilities.

questions.text: Which public-duty claim is directly supported by Section 1-c?

options.text: The architect should observe government laws and ethical standards
The architect may ignore laws when the owner signs a waiver
The architect must advertise every completed project
The architect may claim any specialization after graduation

rationale.correct: Section 1-c requires observing laws, regulations, and ethical standards.
rationale.takeaway: Section 1-c requires observing laws, regulations, and ethical standards.

questions.text: What does Section 1-e say about paid endorsement of building materials?

options.text: It should be avoided; the architect should refrain from paid advertisements endorsing materials or equipment
It is required for all suppliers
It is allowed if the product is expensive
It replaces the client agreement

rationale.correct: Section 1-e bars paid endorsement of construction materials or building equipment.
rationale.takeaway: Section 1-e bars paid endorsement of construction materials or building equipment.

questions.text: Which statement best distinguishes factual public communication from banned publicity?

options.text: Factual materials may be presented when they dignify the profession or advance public knowledge, but paid or misleading publicity is barred
All public communication by architects is banned
All paid advertisements are required
Misleading claims are acceptable if printed

rationale.correct: Section 1-d allows factual material while prohibiting paid, exaggerated, or misleading publicity.
rationale.takeaway: Section 1-d allows factual material while prohibiting paid, exaggerated, or misleading publicity.

options.text: Advance safety, health, well-being, civic service, and heritage concerns
Maximize supplier commissions

questions.text: Which action violates the source rule on professional publications?

options.text: Soliciting advertisements or support for a publication presenting the architect work
Keeping factual project records
Explaining professional standards factually
Sharing non-misleading public knowledge about the architect function

rationale.correct: Section 1-e bars soliciting advertisements or support toward publications presenting the architect work.
rationale.takeaway: Section 1-e bars soliciting advertisements or support toward publications presenting the architect work.

questions.text: Why is "the client approved it" a weak defense in a public-duty scenario?

options.text: Section 1 separately gives the architect civic and public responsibilities
Section 1 makes the client the only ethical authority
Section 1 eliminates laws and regulations
Section 1 concerns only supplier discounts

rationale.correct: The public-duty section is not erased by client approval.
rationale.takeaway: The public-duty section is not erased by client approval.

questions.text: What should a source-safe exam answer avoid in ETH-003?

options.text: Unverified penalty or discipline claims not found in the checked UAP source
The Section 1-a safety duty
The Section 1-f specialization rule
The Section 1-d publicity rule

rationale.correct: The local checked source is the UAP ethics text; unsupported external penalties stay deferred.
rationale.takeaway: The local checked source is the UAP ethics text; unsupported external penalties stay deferred.
